title: Yiwen Zhang
text:
2023–ongoing
The Global Shapers Community Beijing Hub, initiated by the World Economic Forum, is a network of young leaders committed to driving dialogue, action, and change on local and global challenges.
Yiwen Zhang serves as a Global Shaper and Curator, leading initiatives on gender equality, education equity, and youth empowerment — including the flagship project SheShapes, which connects young women with mentors from academia, consulting, and international organizations.





August 2023
Yiwen Zhang was interviewed by United Nations News as a youth delegate of the China SDGs Initiative, sharing her experiences in advancing education equality and gender empowerment.
In the interview, she discussed how young changemakers can translate global goals into local actions and highlighted her work through SheShapes Impact and Future Youth to support girls and students from underprivileged backgrounds.

text:

    中文
  

  
    Research · Policy · Public Action

    
      I study how inequality shapes lives, and how research and public action can help widen opportunity.
    

    
      我关注不平等如何塑造个体命运，也希望通过研究、政策与公共行动，拓宽更多人的机会。
    
  


  
  
    
  

  
    
      张译文
      Yiwen Zhang

I am a PhD student in the Department of Government at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE), affiliated with the Data Science Institute and supervised by Professor Valentino Larcinese. I am fully funded as a first-cohort Enlighten Scholar.


My research sits at the intersection of political economy, public opinion, social policy, and computational social science. I study how inequality shapes political behaviour, how welfare states structure citizens’ redistributive preferences, and how computational methods—including large language models—can be used to study political attitudes and policy-relevant questions.




我本科毕业于北京大学政府管理学院，现为伦敦政治经济学院政府系政治学博士生，同时隶属于数据科学研究所，导师为 Valentino Larcinese 教授。我是 LSE 首届 Enlighten Scholar，博士阶段获得全额资助。


我的研究关注不平等政治经济学、公共舆论、社会政策与计算社会科学之间的交叉问题。我尤其关心：不平等如何影响政治行为，福利国家如何塑造公民的再分配偏好，以及包括大语言模型在内的计算方法如何帮助我们研究政治态度与政策问题。


Before joining LSE, I worked at the International Organization for Migration, where I analysed the UK National Referral Mechanism data and contributed to policy-facing research on modern slavery and human trafficking.

Current research

Welfare states, inequality, and redistributive politics

Public opinion and political psychology

Computational social science and LLM-generated synthetic data

China, the UK, and comparative political economy

As a first-generation university student from Sichuan, China, I am passionate about public welfare and education equity. In my spare time, I enjoy playing football, watching musicals, and hiking.


Selected public work

Co-founder, Future Youth (后浪计划)
Co-founder, SheShapes Social Impact



Education

MPhil in Comparative Politics, Peking University

BA in Politics, Law, and Sociology, Peking University
